Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
626 AM EDT Thu Aug 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 625 AM EDT Thursday...

Have updated the probability of precipitation forecast today to
reflect the current rain sinking south and southeast across
southern Vermont this morning. No major changes were made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 258 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected 
this afternoon as another shortwave moves through the region. 
Conditions turn drier and quieter by Friday and Saturday.

2. Showers with a low chance of thunderstorms are expected late 
Sunday into Monday. Following a dry Tuesday, the next chance of 
showers will come in by Wednesday afternoon.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 258 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Another shortwave is approaching the region early this 
morning, bringing showers and thunderstorms to parts of northern New 
York and Vermont. This wave is expected to move through during the 
day today, with better aligned forcing for our region than 
yesterday. Increasing diurnal instability around 1000-1500 J/kg 
focused around the international border and across the Champlain 
Valley with similar shear profiles to yesterday will bring better 
chances for thunderstorms to the region this afternoon, though a few 
showers may be possible in the mid to late morning with little 
capping inversion present. Some of the more robust high resolution 
models are projecting 2100-2300 J/kg of surface based CAPE, and 
freezing levels have been lower than typical for this time of year. 
Instability will be highest in northern Vermont and the Champlain 
Valley, though showers and thunderstorms anywhere across the 
northern portions of the CWA will be possible tomorrow. Brief gusty 
winds around 40 mph and small hail will be possible. Precipitable 
water values will slightly increase today to near an inch and a 
quarter, with parallel motion and training cells. However, again, 
deep warm cloud depths will be thin with a low risk for any flooding 
concerns. Temperatures today will likely remain on the cooler side 
with highs in the 70s to around 80 F in northwesterly flow. 

Troughing will slide east with surface high pressure building in 
from Canada tonight and Friday. More calm and quiet conditions are 
expected through Saturday night. High temperatures will be slightly 
below seasonal normals in the 70s and lower 80s. Nights will be on 
the cooler side as well with prime radiational cooling conditions 
present and lows in the mid 40s to mid 50s. Radiational fog looks 
increasingly likely in the typical valley spots tonight and Friday 
night, especially in locations that see rainfall today.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Generally no real changes to the expectations for a good 
chance for widespread, beneficial rain late Sunday through Sunday 
night. Probabilities of at least a half inch of rain have ticked up 
from 24 hours ago into the 30 to 50% range, while thunderstorm 
chances remain conditional on a more northward type of low track. 
Among global models, all of the GEFS and GEPS membership shows CAPE 
remaining under 500 J/kg during this event, but a minority of ENS 
members are depicting a wedge of greater instability making 
northward progress into at least northern New York, suggesting at 
least elevated thunderstorms would be possible, enhancing rainfall 
rates at times. Otherwise, we'll have to watch on Monday behind this 
low pressure system if there is enough moisture to work with to have 
some thunderstorm development as a cool front and trough follows 
behind it. For now, greatest potential for thunderstorms Monday is 
in northeastern Vermont, but this portion of the forecast is rather 
uncertain given lack of a strong trigger similar to what we've seen 
in recent days in a fast flow pattern.

Tuesday continues to look largely dry associated with broad ridging. 
Wednesday may start similarly, then take a turn towards more active 
weather with broadly good large scale support for organized showers 
and thunderstorms as the next trough moves in from the west. Given 
we're seven days out and only weak signals for severe weather show 
up in the long range guidance, this is not likely to be a 
significant event but will bear watching if you have outdoor plans. 
Seasonable weather is anticipated through this period, with daytime 
temperatures mainly in the 70s with dewpoints in the 50s, trending a 
only a bit warmer and more humid on Wednesday.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z THURSDAY THROUGH MONDAY/...
Through 06Z Friday...Challenging forecast over the next six hours
with variable conditions at most sites as a thunderstorm complex
gradually slides southeastward through the airspace. This activity
has passed MSS and will move south of EFK. Elsewhere, a direct hit
at SLK is occurring at the start of the period with at least VCTS to
the northeast at PBG and possibly BTV. Convective trends and limited
instability farther east suggest a weakening of thunderstorms as
they move towards MPV and RUT, with no mention of thunder given. The
incoming showers however will limit the otherwise favorable
conditions for dense fog at MPV which are present at the moment.
Therefore have indicated only temporary LIFR conditions for 
most of the period coinciding with the expected rain when 
lowest ceilings should scatter. Following the thunderstorms at 
SLK, would expect a period of low ceilings and mist is possible 
but confidence is low, hence also a TEMPO group was used there. 
Finally, abundant moisture at MSS following the nocturnal 
thunderstorms will lead to a period of low stratus overnight and
into the morning as light winds keep the clouds from mixing out
quickly after sunrise. 

Winds continue to be light and variable through at least 15Z, 
then trend a bit stronger out of the west or northwest 
thereafter, with a few gusts in the 15 to 20 knot range at most 
terminals possible between 18Z and 23Z. Winds should abate after
sunset. While widely scattered showers and thunderstorms are 
possible during the remainder of the period, coverage and timing
are too uncertain to indicate in this set of TAFs beyond the 
first 12 hours.

Outlook...

Friday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. Chance SHRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
